events.title: Bascom Teens Reach Meeting: Canned Food Drive

cases.refreshed: Teens 13-18 are invited to the Bascom Teens Reach Canned Food Drive! Bring canned food to be donated to the needy through Second Harvest of Silicon Valley. No more than ten (10) cans per person, please. Refreshments will be available! Teens are invited to join Bascom Library Teens Reach in-person every 3rd Tuesday of the month! This program features fun volunteer opportunities, craft activities, games, and chances to hang out with your peers and learn new skills and information. To join Teens Reach you must be 13-18 years of age, have a strong interest in the library, enjoy working with people of all ages and cultures, and be willing to learn new skills. Membership requires regular attendance at meetings, participation in and support of library activities and events, and a sense of fun and adventure. As a bonus, Teens Reach members can earn community service hours through participation in meetings and activities. For more information go to: www.SJPL.org/teensReach For ages 13-18. Held in Group Study Room 2. Registration recommended but not required.

events.title: Career Communication Series: Interviewing with confidence: Managing your emotions in the interview process

cases.refreshed: Most of us probably have been nervous going into an interview. Have you gone to an interview fully prepared and then gotten overwhelmed with the experience? We can help you project confidence in the interview process! We will provide strategies for handling uncertainty and stress during interviews, and then help you practice those strategies through real world situations. In partnership with SJSU Department of Communication Studies This program is followed immediately by: Becoming an effective team player Free. No registration required. Parking validation for the garage at 88 S. 4th Street will be provided at the program. E-newsletter Signup: Get the inside scoop on business and career resources at SJPL. Sign up today for our monthly e-newsletter, highlighting the latest programs, e-resources and services available at the San José Public Library. #sjplworkscareer

events.title: Career Communication Series: Becoming an Effective Team Player

cases.refreshed: Most work requires you to coordinate and communicate effectively within a team. The ability to work with others is a skill that can make a difference in your career. In this workshop we will help you develop strategies for working effectively in teams. We will emphasize strategies for reducing conflict and miscommunication with your team members and how to help your team achieve its goals. This program is immediately preceded by Interviewing with confidence: Managing your emotions in the interview process In partnership with SJSU Department of Communication Studies Free. cases.refreshed: Join our Readers' Book Club to share the joy of reading and to expand your reading horizons. We will read thought-provoking adult fiction of various genres for readers of different ages and backgrounds. Join us in reading our last title of the year: The Teacher of Nomad Land by Daniel Nayeri What to Expect: For November, we will be reading The Teacher of Nomad Land by Daniel Nayeri, a children's book and a National Book Award winner, which recounts the story of a young man who takes his father's job as the teacher of nomads to survive the war. In the backdrop of World War II, Babak and his little sister must make a trek through the mountains. Read this book to discover Babak's fate and to learn the language of a foreign culture and landscape. Then come and share with us your thoughts and discoveries.

cases.refreshed: Ready for some friendly competition? Bring your friends and family for a fun game of Bingo and the chance to win awesome book prizes! We will be running multiple rounds, so you can drop in and play anytime. Don't miss your chance to shout "Bingo!" and take home a new favorite book. No registration required, space available on a first-come, first-served basis. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

cases.refreshed: English as a Second Language (ESL) / Learn English: Beyond the Basics is an in-person 8-week class with lessons on English grammar, pronunciation, and idioms. It is for adult (18 years and older) intermediate and advanced English learners who can have a conversation in English and want to improve their pronunciation and understanding. To register for the entire 8-week series, please include your email address and make sure it is entered correctly. Please register only once for the entire series. Please note: Registration closes on the 3rd week of class; Registrants who do not the 1st class may be unregistered, If you cannot attend the 1st class, please email Priya Murthy at priya.murthy@paloalto.gov.
